## Welcome!

I am a Ph.D. student in Political Science at Florida State University, specializing in International Relations and Comparative Politics. My research examines how political elites use rhetorical strategies to respond to (or generate) international crises, legitimize power, and shape public perceptions amid democratic backsliding and global instability. I focus on elite framing effects and democratic accountability in shifting international contexts, asking how leaders mobilize public support during crises and how these strategies can accelerate or constrain democratic erosion.

I also teach courses in international relations and quantitative social science methodology at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. I aim to foster an environment for curious and critical thinking about global issues, blending both empirical testing and traditional theoretical explanations.

If you are curious about my work, please explore my page! If you have any questions or would like to reach out, please contact me at the links provided.
